### `todo_app_tasks`

Core task entity representing individual todo items managed by users.

Tasks form the fundamental units of work in the todo application,
containing essential information needed for task completion tracking and
organization. Each task belongs to a specific user and can be associated
with categories and completion records.

The task lifecycle includes states: pending (default), in-progress, and
completed. Tasks support prioritization through Low, Medium, and High
levels, with Low as the default priority to minimize decision friction.
Users can add optional due dates and belong to categories for
organization.

Task creation emphasizes minimal required information - only a title is
mandatory - with optional fields for descriptions, due dates, priorities,
and categories. This design supports rapid task capture while providing
flexibility for detailed planning when desired.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_user_id`: Task creator's [todo_app_users.id](#todo_app_users)
- `todo_app_category_id`
  > Task's [todo_app_categories.id](#todo_app_categories). Links tasks to categories for
  > organization
- `title`
  > Task title between 1-200 characters. The essential task description
  > required for creation.
- `description`
  > Optional task description up to 2,000 characters providing additional
  > context or instructions
- `status`: Task lifecycle status: pending (default), in-progress, or completed
- `priority`
  > Task priority level: Low (default), Medium, or High used for sorting and
  > visual distinction
- `due_date`
  > Optional due date for task completion. Validates to prevent past dates
  > and limits to 1 year in future
- `completion_order`
  > Manual sort order for task positioning within user's preferred
  > organization
- `created_at`: Task creation timestamp
- `updated_at`: Last modification timestamp

### `todo_app_categories`

User-defined organizational categories for grouping related tasks.

Categories provide a hierarchical organization system enabling users to
group tasks by project, context, or any classification scheme they
choose. Each category belongs to a specific user and contains any number
of associated tasks.

Category names must be unique within user accounts and conform to
character restrictions to ensure system compatibility. The system limits
users to 50 categories maximum to prevent over-complexity while providing
sufficient organizational flexibility.

Categories support flexible organization patterns including work/personal
divisions, project-based groupings, or contextual organization schemes.
Users can filter tasks by category and perform bulk operations on all
tasks within a category.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_user_id`: Category creator's [todo_app_users.id](#todo_app_users)
- `name`
  > Category name between 2-50 characters using only letters, numbers,
  > spaces, and hyphens
- `description`
  > Optional category description providing context about the category's
  > purpose
- `created_at`: Category creation timestamp
- `updated_at`: Last modification timestamp

### `todo_app_task_completions`

Record of task completion events capturing when tasks are marked complete.

This table tracks the completion lifecycle of tasks, providing
accountability and enabling completion statistics calculation. Each
completion record represents a unique completion event with timestamps
and optional completion notes.

The system supports task reopening by maintaining completion history even
when tasks are later reactivated. This allows for productivity analytics
including completion rates, time-to-completion, and streak tracking.

Completion records are created when tasks transition to completed status
and maintain references back to the original task. Users can add
completion notes to document how tasks were accomplished or any relevant
outcomes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_task_id`: Reference to [todo_app_tasks.id](#todo_app_tasks) for the completed task
- `todo_app_user_id`: Reference to [todo_app_users.id](#todo_app_users) of the user who completed the task
- `completed_at`: Timestamp when the task was marked complete
- `notes`: Optional notes explaining how the task was completed or any outcomes
- `completion_order`: Order of completion for sorting purposes within user's completion history
- `reactivated`: Flag indicating if this completion was followed by task reactivation
- `created_at`: Completion record creation timestamp
- `reactivated_at`: Timestamp when task was subsequently reactivated if applicable

### `todo_app_task_audit_logs`

Historical audit trail capturing all modifications to tasks for
accountability and recovery.

This table serves as the complete change log for all task operations
including creation, updates, completion, category changes, and other
modifications. Each entry represents a specific action performed on a
task with detailed change tracking.

Audit logs support compliance requirements, provide change history for
user reference, and enable system administrators to monitor task
lifecycle patterns for improvements. The snapshot approach ensures
historical data integrity even as tasks are modified or deleted.

Every task modification creates a new audit log entry capturing the
before-and-after state information. This design supports comprehensive
change tracking while maintaining optimal performance for current task
operations by separating historical data.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_task_id`: Reference to [todo_app_tasks.id](#todo_app_tasks) being audited
- `todo_app_user_id`: Reference to [todo_app_users.id](#todo_app_users) who performed the action
- `action`
  > Type of action performed: CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, COMPLETE, REACTIVATE,
  > MOVE, etc.
- `field_changes`: JSON representation of field changes made during this action
- `old_value`: Previous value for fields that changed (for single-field changes)
- `new_value`: New value for fields that changed (for single-field changes)
- `created_at`: Audit log entry timestamp when the action occurred

### `todo_app_user_quotas`

Individual user quota limits and usage tracking for business rule
enforcement.

Tracks each user's consumption against predefined limits like maximum
tasks (1000), categories (100), and other resource allocations. Supports
both hard limits that prevent further usage and soft limits that trigger
warnings.

The quota system prevents system abuse while providing fair resource
allocation across all users. Usage metrics are updated atomically to
ensure accuracy during high-concurrency scenarios.

Quotas can be configured per user to provide premium features or
accommodate special requirements while maintaining system integrity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_user_id`: User who owns these quota limits. [todo_app_users.id](#todo_app_users)
- `max_tasks`
  > Maximum number of tasks allowed for this user. Default 1000 for standard
  > users.
- `max_categories`
  > Maximum number of custom categories allowed. Default 100 for standard
  > users.
- `max_daily_task_creations`: Maximum tasks that can be created per day. Default 30 to prevent spam.
- `current_task_count`
  > Current number of tasks this user has created. Updated atomically on task
  > operations.
- `current_category_count`: Current number of categories created by this user.
- `daily_task_creation_count`: Number of tasks created today by this user. Resets at midnight.
- `is_premium`
  > Whether this user has premium quota allowances. Premium users get higher
  > limits.
- `quota_reset_date`: Date when daily quotas will reset. Used for tracking daily limits.
- `created_at`: When these quota settings were established.
- `updated_at`: Last modification time for any quota setting.

### `todo_app_rate_limits`

System-wide rate limiting configuration and enforcement tracking.

Manages rate limit rules for different API endpoints and user actions.
Tracks both global rate limits (per IP, per endpoint) and user-specific
limits to prevent abuse and ensure fair usage.

The rate limiting system implements sliding window counters with
automatic reset mechanisms. Different endpoints can have different rate
limits based on their resource consumption and frequency patterns.

Supports both authenticated user limits and anonymous IP-based
restrictions to protect the system from various attack vectors while
maintaining legitimate user access.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_user_id`
  > Optional user associated with this rate limit. Null for global or
  > IP-based limits. [todo_app_users.id](#todo_app_users)
- `limit_name`
  > Descriptive name for this rate limit rule. Examples: 'task_creation',
  > 'user_registration', 'guest_access'.
- `endpoint_pattern`
  > API endpoint pattern this limit applies to. Supports wildcards for
  > pattern matching.
- `request_limit`: Maximum number of requests allowed within the time window.
- `time_window_seconds`
  > Time window in seconds for the rate limit. Common values: 60, 300, 3600,
  > 86400.
- `current_request_count`
  > Current request count within the active time window. Resets automatically
  > when window expires.
- `window_start_time`
  > Start time of the current rate limit window. Used for sliding window
  > calculations.
- `identifier_type`
  > Type of identifier for this rate limit. Values: 'user_id', 'ip_address',
  > 'global'.
- `identifier_value`: The actual identifier value. Could be user ID, IP address, or 'global'.
- `is_active`: Whether this rate limit rule is currently active and being enforced.
- `created_at`: When this rate limit rule was created.
- `updated_at`: Last modification time for this rate limit rule.

### `todo_app_constraint_definitions`

Business rule and validation constraint definitions for the todo
application.

Stores the specification for all business rules including data
validation, format requirements, computational limits, and operational
constraints applied throughout the system.

Each constraint definition includes validation logic, error messages,
enforcement mechanisms, and applicability scope. Constraints can be
global (system-wide) or contextual (applied based on conditions).

This centralized constraint management enables business rules to be
modified without code changes while maintaining consistency across all
system operations.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `constraint_name`

  > code and logs.
- `constraint_type`
  > Type of constraint. Values: 'validation', 'limit', 'format',
  > 'business_rule'.
- `applicable_scope`
  > Where this constraint applies. Values: 'global', 'user', 'guest',
  > 'task_creation', 'authentication'.
- `constraint_definition`
  > JSON or structured definition of the constraint rule. Stores validation
  > logic, format patterns, or business rule specifications.
- `error_message_template`
  > Template for error messages when this constraint is violated. Can include

- `is_enforced`
  > Whether this constraint is currently being enforced. Allows soft

- `severity_level`
  > Severity when violated. Values: 'error' (blocks operation), 'warning'

operations.specification: User registration operation for creating new authenticated user accounts. This operation handles the creation of new users in the todo_app_users table with email and password fields. Users must provide a unique email address and password that meets security requirements. The operation generates initial access and refresh tokens upon successful registration.
operations.description:
This operation creates a new authenticated user account in the todo application system. Users register by providing a valid email address and secure password, which are stored in the todo_app_users table along with automated timestamps for account creation and modification tracking.

The email field enforces uniqueness across all registered accounts and follows standard email validation formats to ensure deliverability and system integrity. Password security is maintained through secure hashing before storage, ensuring credentials are protected according to modern security standards.

Upon successful registration, the system immediately issues JWT access and refresh tokens that enable authenticated access to all todo management functionality including task creation, organization, and completion tracking. These tokens are returned in the authorization response and should be stored by the client application for subsequent API calls.

This operation serves as the primary entry point for new users joining the todo application ecosystem, providing immediate access to personal task management capabilities while establishing the foundation for secure session management and user-specific data isolation.

Related operations include the user login endpoint for existing account authentication and the token refresh endpoint for maintaining ongoing access without requiring repeated credential entry.

This operation validates email and password credentials against the todo_app_users table and issues new access and refresh tokens upon successful authentication. operations.description:
This operation handles user authentication for existing accounts in the todo application. Users provide their registered email address and password for credential verification against stored data in the todo_app_users table.

The authentication process validates the provided email exists in the system and verifies the password hash against the securely stored credential using modern cryptographic methods. Upon successful validation, the system issues new JWT access and refresh tokens with updated expiration times to maintain secure session management.

Access tokens provide temporary authorization for API calls requiring user authentication, while refresh tokens enable session renewal without requiring repeated credential entry, supporting convenient user experience while maintaining security standards.

The login operation establishes authenticated context for accessing protected todo management endpoints including task creation, modification, completion tracking, and personal organization features. All subsequent operations require valid access tokens generated through this authentication flow.

Login attempts are logged for security monitoring, and the system implements appropriate rate limiting to prevent brute force attacks while maintaining reasonable access for legitimate users experiencing temporary authentication difficulties.

This operation is essential for applications where users engage with todo functionality over extended periods, as it maintains session continuity without interrupting workflow for repeated authentication requirements. The system ensures token renewal requests originate from authenticated contexts and implements appropriate security measures to prevent token hijacking or unauthorized session extension.

Token refresh operations integrate with the complete authentication lifecycle, supporting seamless transitions between access token expiration and continued authenticated usage without disrupting user experience or requiring manual re-authentication interruptions.

This operation enables authenticated users to search and retrieve their personal tasks with advanced filtering capabilities. The operation queries the todo_app_tasks table and returns paginated results based on the user's search criteria and access permissions.

Users can filter tasks by completion status, category assignment, priority levels, creation date ranges, and perform keyword searches within task titles and descriptions. The operation supports complex combinations of filter criteria, allowing users to build precise queries for finding specific subsets of their task inventory efficiently.

Pagination is fully supported with configurable page sizes, allowing users to efficiently browse through large task collections. Results can be sorted by various fields including creation date, due date, priority levels, completion status, or category assignment in both ascending and descending order based on user preferences.

User isolation is enforced through the provider layer and JWT token validation, ensuring each user can only query tasks they have created. No user-to-user task visibility is allowed without explicit permission configuration.

This operation integrates seamlessly with the task management workflow and supports various client interfaces including web dashboard views, mobile task lists, and integration scenarios that require efficient task querying capabilities for productivity-focused user experiences. operations.description:
Create a new todo task in the authenticated user's personal todo list. This operation supports rapid task creation with only a title required, while providing flexibility for detailed task planning through optional fields.

Required field is title (1-200 characters) which forms the essential task description required for creation as defined in the todo_app_tasks table. Optional fields include description (up to 2,000 characters providing detailed instructions), due_date (must be in the future, limited to 1 year ahead as per Prisma validation), priority level (Low/Medium/High with Low as default), and category assignment (must link to an existing todo_app_category that belongs to the authenticated user via todo_app_category_id).

The operation validates business rules from the CrudOperation object: title length constraints (1-200 characters), due_date must be future-dated within reasonable range (now to +1 year), priority must be a valid option (Low/Medium/High), and category must belong to the authenticated user through foreign key validation on todo_app_category_id.

Task creation follows the rapid capture philosophy - supporting one-click task addition while allowing users to elaborate later through the update operation. The completion_order field automatically assigns positioning within the user's preferred task organization system. The operation sets both created_at and updated_at timestamps automatically during task creation.

ITodoAppTask.description:
Core task entity representing individual todo items managed by users in the application.

Tasks form the fundamental units of work in the todo system, containing essential information needed for effective task tracking and organization. Each task belongs to a specific user and can optionally be associated with categories for better organization and filtration.

The task lifecycle includes statuses of pending, in-progress, and completed, with visual distinctions for priority levels. Optional due dates provide deadline management while the manual completion order supports custom task organization preferences. The design emphasizes minimal required information with title being the only mandatory field, supporting rapid task capture while providing flexibility for detailed planning.

title.description: Task title between 1-200 characters. The essential description required for creating actionable todo items. This field supports the rapid task capture philosophy by requiring only basic task identification. Users can immediately start organizing tasks with meaningful names while maintaining the ability to add details through optional fields.

description.description: Optional task description up to 2,000 characters providing additional context or instructions for task completion. This field enables detailed task planning when users require comprehensive guidance or supporting information. The description supports markdown formatting and can include step-by-step instructions, necessary resources, or helpful context that enhances task completion success rates.

todo_app_category_id.description: Optional category reference for task organization by linking to existing todo_app_categories.id. Allows tasks to be grouped with similar items for better organization and filtering. This foreign key enables users to create structured task hierarchies and apply efficient filtering strategies across their personal task management system. Categories must be owned by the authenticated user for proper access control.

oneOf.description: Task priority level for sorting and visual distinction. Low priority represents standard task importance suitable for routine activities not critical to immediate user goals. This ordering enables users to focus attention on higher priorities while maintaining comprehensive task tracking.

Task priority level for sorting and visual distinction. Medium priority indicates tasks requiring attention but not immediate action. This priority level supports balanced workload management by highlighting moderately important tasks while distinguishing from both low-priority routine activities and high-priority urgent items.

Task priority level for sorting and visual distinction. High priority identifies tasks requiring immediate attention and completion. This priority designation supports urgent task identification and helps users prioritize their workday by surfacing critical activities that directly impact user objectives or deadlines.

priority.description: Task priority level for sorting and visual distinction across the user's task portfolio. The priority system enables efficient workload triage by providing visual cues and sorting capabilities. Low priority serves as the system default to minimize decision friction during rapid task capture while allowing users to escalate urgency when appropriate.

due_date.description: Optional due date for task completion supporting user deadline management and planning workflows. Must be in the future and within 1 year from current date to maintain realistic planning horizons. This temporal constraint ensures users can effectively schedule tasks while avoiding overwhelming future commitments or impractical deadline planning that could reduce task completion rates.

oneOf.description: Manual sort order for task positioning within user's task list organization system. When not explicitly provided, current timestamp is applied automatically to maintain chronological task ordering within the user's preferred organizational framework.

completion_order.description: Manual sort order for task positioning within the user's preferred organizational system. This field enables users to control displayed task ordering based on personal workflow preferences rather than relying solely on creation or due date sequencing. The system automatically applies current timestamp if not specified, ensuring consistent task presentation and maintaining the user's organizational context during rapid task creation workflows.

ITodoAppTask.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating new tasks in the todo application supporting the rapid capture philosophy while providing comprehensive organizational capabilities. Authentication context (user) is managed through JWT authorization, ensuring secure task ownership assignment without exposing system user identification fields.

This DTO represents the essential business information required for effective task creation while preventing authentication bypass vulnerabilities. The design emphasizes immediate task capture with minimal required information - only the title is mandatory - while supporting advanced features like categorization, prioritization, and deadline management for comprehensive personal task management needs. User authentication context cannot be specified in request body and is derived from verified JWT token.

The implementation validates all input data against comprehensive business rules including length constraints, temporal validation, and foreign key relationships. Optional organizational features like categories, priorities, and due dates enable users to build sophisticated task hierarchies without overwhelming the initial creation process. Authentication context is automatically applied server-side from verified user session without exposing internal user identification systems.

oneOf.description: Updated task title between 1-200 characters maintaining the essential task identification requirements. Title updates support evolving task understanding and refined task descriptions while preserving the minimal essential information needed for effective task management and completion tracking.

title.description: Updated task title supporting evolving understanding and refined task descriptions. Must maintain non-empty constraint to preserve task clarity and actionability. This enables users to improve task descriptions as project requirements become clearer while maintaining backward compatibility and preserving existing task completion tracking.

description.description: Updated task description up to 2,000 characters supporting detailed planning and instruction improvement. Users can enhance task guidance by adding comprehensive context or instructions that improve task completion probability while supporting null assignment to remove existing descriptions when they are no longer relevant or helpful to task completion workflows.

todo_app_category_id.description: Updated category reference enabling task reorganization or null assignment to remove existing category associations. This field supports user organizational preference evolution and accommodates changing project structures or workflow adjustments without requiring task recreation or data duplication in the system.

oneOf.description: Resets task to initial pending state indicating awaiting action or attention. Supports task lifecycle management and provides clean slate for tasks requiring fresh approach or interruption recovery.

Marks task as actively being worked on indicating current user focus and effort investment. This status enables tracking of ongoing active work while distinguishing from both pending tasks requiring initial attention and completed tasks finished successfully.

Indicates successful task completion and goal achievement within the user's task management workflow. This status enables completion tracking, statistical analysis, and provides positive reinforcement through demonstrated productivity metrics and goal accomplishment evidence.

status.description: Updated task status for comprehensive lifecycle management supporting various workflow transitions and user organizational needs. Status changes enable task prioritization adjustment, interruption recovery, and completion tracking while maintaining user accountability and progress visibility within their personal task management system.

priority.description: Updated task priority level for dynamic workload adjustment and importance reassessment. Users can adjust priorities based on changing circumstances, shifting deadlines, or evolution of project relevance while maintaining the three-tier sorting system that enables efficient task visibility and attention allocation strategies.

due_date.description: Updated due date supporting deadline management evolution or removal of existing deadlines. Must follow date validation rules ensuring realistic planning timelines. This flexibility enables users to adjust schedules based on changing project requirements, resource availability, or shifting priority landscapes while maintaining system constraint compliance.

oneOf.description: Updated manual sort order enabling refined task positioning within user's evolving organizational framework and workflow preferences. Supports dynamic task organization as users develop preferences and adapt systems to changing productivity needs.

completion_order.description: Updated manual sort order enabling refined task positioning within user's evolving organizational preferences. This field supports dynamic task organization as users develop new workflow strategies and adapt their task management approach to changing productivity needs and project complexity.

Users can adjust task details based on evolving understanding while the system enforces task ownership immutability for security protection.

ITodoAppUser.IRefresh.description:
Token refresh request for renewing expired access tokens. Supports continued authenticated access to todo management endpoints without requiring re-authentication with credentials.

This operation uses valid refresh tokens to generate new access tokens while maintaining authenticated user sessions. The refresh mechanism balances user convenience with security by eliminating the need for repeated credential entry during normal application usage.

Session context fields enable security tracking and session lineage documentation in the todo_app_user_sessions table. Tracking token refresh activity helps identify legitimate session continuations versus potential security threats.

The refresh operation is essential for maintaining continuous authenticated access during extended todo management sessions where users engage with task creation, modification, completion tracking, and organizational features over time periods longer than access token expiration.

User email address used for account authentication and communication. Must be unique across all registered users and follow standard email format validation.

This field supports the soft delete pattern where account data is preserved for audit trails, recovery scenarios, and compliance requirements while maintaining data integrity and system performance optimization.

The schema has been security-reviewed to remove all authentication-sensitive fields while maintaining necessary operational data. ID, email, and timestamps are provided for legitimate application functionality without compromising security boundaries or exposing credential material.

ITodoAppGuest.IRefresh.description:
Guest token refresh request for extending temporary guest session duration while maintaining security integrity and comprehensive session tracking.

Represents the credential refresh payload that enables continued temporary access for guest users exploring application features without full registration commitment. Contains connection context information required for session renewal, security validation, and audit trail maintenance during the refresh process.

This request structure ensures guest sessions can be extended appropriately while maintaining session boundaries, preventing indefinite access, and supporting eventual transition to full registered accounts. The operation balances security requirements with user experience by allowing temporary session remediation while implementing strict time limits and access controls.

Usage across guest authentication flows supports temporary user exploration, conversion optimization, and security protection through session lifecycle management that enforces appropriate usage restrictions while providing legitimate feature exploration opportunities.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring. Captures the requesting client's network location for audit trails, geolocation filtering, and abuse detection.

Supports both IPv4 and IPv6 format addresses. Optional field that can be extracted from HTTP headers when not explicitly provided by the client. Mandatory in certain contexts requiring enhanced security validation or when server-side rendering obscures source IP information.

The address is used for security monitoring, session correlation, geographic restriction enforcement, and compliance requirements including location-based data handling regulations.

href.description:
Connection URL or current page location when the guest session refresh request was initiated. Essential for session tracking, security monitoring, and location-aware authentication.

Contains the complete URI including protocol, domain, path, and query parameters representing the guest user's current application state at the time of token refresh. Used to verify session continuity, detect unauthorized geographic shifts, and maintain session context across refresh cycles.

This persistent location tracking enables legitimate refresh requests while preventing session hijacking attempts that could occur if requests originate from unexpected web locations or geographic regions inconsistent with the established guest session profile.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating how the guest arrived at the application or the source that motivated session refresh. Provides user flow analysis, marketing attribution, and session origin verification for comprehensive audit tracking and session management.

Contains the complete URI of the referring page, document, or resource that directed the guest user to initiate refresh traffic. Supports marketing analytics, conversion tracking across different traffic sources, and early detection of abuse patterns that might indicate automated or illegitimate access attempts.

The referrer enables session origin correlation, user journey mapping, external source validation, and security monitoring to distinguish between legitimate user activity and potential automated session exploitation attempts during the guest token renewal process.

The category system enforces naming conventions and uniqueness constraints while supporting up to 50 categories per user to prevent over-complexity. Users can filter tasks by category and perform bulk operations on all tasks within a category, making organization efficient and intuitive.

ITodoAppTaskCompletionRateStatistics.description:
Task completion rate statistics for authenticated user, calculated as the percentage of completed tasks relative to total tasks created.

This entity represents productivity metrics that aggregate data across the user's task history to provide insights into personal task management effectiveness. The statistics provide quantitative measures of user productivity patterns and completion consistency.

The completion rate is computed using the formula: (Completed Tasks ÷ Total Tasks) × 100. Completed tasks include those marked as complete through the system's completion workflow, while total tasks encompass all tasks created by the user.

These statistics support productivity analysis, enabling users to identify trends, set improvement targets, and monitor progress toward achieving better task completion rates. The calculation accounts for task reactivation scenarios where completed tasks are later reopened for additional work.

total_tasks.description: Total number of tasks created by the authenticated user across all time periods. This count includes all tasks regardless of completion status, providing the denominator for completion rate calculations.

completed_tasks.description: Number of tasks that have been marked as complete by the authenticated user. This count includes all completion events from the task completion history, providing the numerator for completion rate calculations.

incomplete_tasks.description: Number of tasks that are currently pending completion or in progress. This count represents unfinished work and is calculated as total_tasks minus completed_tasks.

completion_rate_percent.description: Task completion rate expressed as a percentage, calculated as (completed_tasks ÷ total_tasks) × 100. This metric provides insight into personal productivity and task management effectiveness.

constraintRule.description: Complete validation rule context defining what operation or data field this limit controls, supporting administrative monitoring and quota management interfaces. Transformed from constraint_rule_id foreign key to provide rule details immediately including rule key, validation type, and field target for comprehensive administrative understanding.

limit_value.description: Current numerical limit value representing the maximum allowance for the targeted operation or resource, displayed in administrative interfaces for quota monitoring and user communication about system constraints

limit_type.description: Type of limit being enforced (e.g., 'task_count', 'category_count', 'bulk_operation_size', 'api_rate'). Defines what resource is being limited.

period_type.description: Time period for which this limit applies (e.g., 'lifetime', 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly'). Determines how limits reset or accumulate.

description.description: Human-readable description providing clear explanation of what this limit controls, its purpose in the system, and practical implications for users.

is_active.description: Boolean status indicating whether this user limit is currently being enforced by the application, supporting administrative toggling of limits for maintenance, testing, or policy adjustments without data deletion

created_at.description: Timestamp when this user limit was created or customized for this user. Tracks when limits were established.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this user limit was last modified. Tracks changes to user-specific limits over time.

ITodoAppValidationRule.ISummary.description:
A summary representation of a validation rule used for administrative interfaces and system configuration displays.

This summary DTO provides essential identification and status information about validation rules without exposing the detailed constraint definitions or implementation specifics. It offers sufficient information for administrative dashboards, rule management interfaces, and system configuration displays where complete rule details are not immediately necessary.

The design emphasizes read-only administrative functionality, presenting rule identification, application scope, and operational status while maintaining privacy of internal validation logic through controlled data exposure appropriate for summary usage scenarios. Rules help ensure data integrity and consistent validation across the todo application.

id.description: Primary key identifier for this validation rule record, providing stable reference for administrative operations, rule management workflows, and system configuration updates

rule_name.description: Human-readable name for this validation rule. Displayed in administrative interfaces for rule identification and used in user-facing error messages. Provides clear label distinguishing this rule from others in rule management workflows.

rule_key.description: Technical identifier reference used by application logic to invoke this specific validation rule programmatically. Enables code-based rule application and error handling within the todo application's validation framework.

validation_type.description: Type classification of validation defining how this rule is applied and evaluated by the system. Categorizations include length limits, format requirements, range constraints, and custom business logic validations that determine application behavior.

field_target.description: Target field or data type this rule validates, expressed using dot notation (e.g., task.title, user.email) to precisely identify the application scope and enable accurate rule application during data validation workflows.

error_message_template.description: Template for error messages generated when validation fails, supporting placeholders for field names and constraint values. Used for consistent user notification and helps developers understand rule applications and failure scenarios.

priority.description: Execution priority order between different rules that might apply to the same field. Lower numbers execute first, enabling rule ordering for complex validation scenarios where rule precedence affects validation outcomes and user experience.

is_active.description: Boolean status indicating whether this validation rule is currently enforced during data validation operations. Supports administrative rule management through enabled/disabled toggles for maintenance, testing, and gradual rollout scenarios.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this validation rule was created. Tracks when rules were introduced into the system.

IError.ISummary.description: Summary error information containing essential details for user notification and system logging. Provides context about which specific task encountered problems during the bulk operation process.

code.description: Error code identifier used for consistent error categorization and handling

message.description: Human-readable error message describing what went wrong during the operation

task_id.description: ID of the specific task that failed during the bulk deletion operation

ITodoAppUserQuota.description:
Comprehensive user quota information including system limits, current usage metrics, and premium status for resource management and monitoring.

This entity represents the complete quota profile for individual users, tracking consumption against predefined limits for tasks, categories, and daily creation rates. The quota system ensures fair resource allocation while preventing system abuse through comprehensive usage tracking.

Quota limits include maximum tasks (default 1000), categories (default 100), and daily task creation limits (default 30) with automatic tracking of current consumption. Premium users receive enhanced limits based on their subscription tier, providing additional capacity for power users.

The system implements both hard limits that prevent further usage when reached, and soft limits that trigger warnings while allowing continued access. Usage metrics are updated atomically to ensure accuracy during high-concurrency scenarios and maintain data integrity across all quota enforcement operations.

This data is crucial for support investigations, usage trend analysis, and ensuring system stability by preventing any single user from consuming excessive resources. Administrators can monitor quota consumption patterns to identify users who might benefit from premium upgrades or require quota adjustments.

id.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for this quota record in the system.

todo_app_user_id.description: User who owns these quota limits. Links to {@link todo_app_users.id} table via foreign key relationship. Required for quota enforcement and user-specific resource allocation.

max_tasks.description: Maximum number of tasks allowed for this user. Default 1000 for standard users, with higher limits for premium subscribers.

max_categories.description: Maximum number of custom categories allowed. Default 100 for standard users, with premium users receiving expanded capacity.

max_daily_task_creations.description: Maximum tasks that can be created per day. Default 30 to prevent spam while allowing legitimate daily productivity workflows.

current_task_count.description: Current number of tasks this user has created. Updated atomically on task operations to ensure accurate quota enforcement.

current_category_count.description: Current number of categories created by this user. Tracks consumption against the max_categories limit.

daily_task_creation_count.description: Number of tasks created today by this user. Resets at midnight for daily quota enforcement.

is_premium.description: Whether this user has premium quota allowances. Premium users get higher limits and enhanced features.

oneOf.description: Date when daily quotas will reset. Used for tracking daily limits and enforcing daily creation restrictions.

quota_reset_date.description: Date when daily quotas will reset. Used for tracking daily limits and enforcing daily creation restrictions.

created_at.description: When these quota settings were established. Provides audit trail for quota configuration changes.

updated_at.description: Last modification time for any quota setting. Tracks when limits were adjusted or usage counters updated.

user.description: Associated user information providing complete context about the quota owner.

ITodoAppTask.IBulkUpdateCategory.description:
Request payload for bulk updating category assignments across multiple tasks simultaneously.

Enables efficient task organization by allowing users to reassign multiple tasks to a different category in a single operation. This atomic update ensures all selected tasks are successfully updated or none are modified in case of errors.

The operation validates that the target category exists and belongs to the authenticated user before executing updates, preventing unauthorized category assignments or accidental data corruption. Task ownership is automatically verified through the authenticated user's context.

Rate limiting applies to prevent bulk update abuse and maintain system performance during high-concurrency scenarios. The operation logs bulk activity for audit purposes while providing immediate feedback about successful updates.

This functionality supports powerful organization workflows where users can select multiple tasks across different views and reassign them to appropriate categories simultaneously, significantly improving the user experience for large-scale task organization projects.

task_ids.description: Array of task identifiers to update. Must contain at least one task ID and no more than 100 tasks to prevent excessive bulk operations.

todo_app_category_id.description: Target category identifier where tasks will be reassigned. Must be a valid category owned by the authenticated user.

pagination.description: Base pagination and search controls including page number, limit, and optional text search.

oneOf.description: Filter to show only specific types of limits (e.g., 'task_count', 'category_count', 'bulk_operation_size'). Use to narrow results to relevant limit categories.

limitType.description: Filter to show only specific types of limits (e.g., 'task_count', 'category_count', 'bulk_operation_size'). Use to narrow results to relevant limit categories.

oneOf.description: Filter by time period scope (e.g., 'lifetime', 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly'). Used to limit results to specific time-based quota categories.

periodType.description: Filter by time period scope (e.g., 'lifetime', 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly'). Used to limit results to specific time-based quota categories.

oneOf.description: Filter by activation status of user limits. True for active limits only, false for inactive, null for all.

isActive.description: Filter by activation status of user limits. True for active limits only, false for inactive, null for all.

ITodoAppUserLimit.IRequest.description:
Extended pagination request for user limit queries with entity-specific filtering.

Builds upon the base pagination structure to add user limit-specific filters including limit type, period type, and activation status. This enables sophisticated querying of user quotas and constraints while maintaining consistent pagination patterns across the application.

ITodoAppSystemSettings.ISummary.description:
A summary view of system configuration settings for administrative management and operational monitoring.

This condensed representation provides key identification, current status, and scope information for system settings while avoiding detailed configuration data that's better displayed in full detail views.

Used for administrative dashboard displays and configuration overview interfaces where rapid system status identification is needed.

id.description: Primary identifier for this system settings record

setting_key.description: Unique technical identifier for configuration value retrieval

setting_value.description: Current configuration value. Can be string/number/json serialized as needed

setting_type.description: Data type classification (string, number, boolean, json) for application parsing

is_active.description: Current activation status. Active settings are used by the application

description.description: Human-readable description explaining the setting's purpose and control scope

page.description: Page number for pagination. Defaults to 1 if not specified. Used to navigate through large result sets efficiently.

limit.description: Number of items per page. Defaults to 10 if not specified, with a maximum of 100 to prevent performance issues.

search.description: Search query to filter settings by key, value, or description. Supports partial matching to help locate specific configuration items efficiently.

setting_type.description: Filter settings by their data type classification. Useful for grouping related configuration items (e.g., show only 'boolean' or 'number' settings).

is_active.description: Filter settings by their active status. When true, shows only active settings. When false, shows only inactive settings. When omitted, shows all settings.

environment_scope.description: Filter settings by deployment environment scope. Useful for viewing settings specific to development, staging, or production environments.

ITodoAppSystemSettings.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for filtering and paginating system configuration settings.

This DTO provides flexible query capabilities for system administrators to efficiently locate and manage configuration settings. It supports text-based search across setting keys, values, and descriptions, as well as filtering by status, type, and environment scope.

The request parameters are designed to work together for advanced filtering scenarios. For example, administrators can search for specific types of settings while limiting results to particular environments or active/inactive status for efficient system management.

ITodoAppTaskId.description: Represents a single task identifier within bulk operations. Contains the UUID4 identifier for todo application tasks that are part of larger bulk processing workflows. This lightweight identifier type enables efficient task identification without carrying full task metadata across bulk operations, reducing payload size while maintaining precise task targeting for bulk actions.

id.description: UUID4 identifier for a specific todo application task. Required for precise task targeting during bulk operations across the authenticated user's task list.

page.description: Page number for paginated results, starting from 1. Used to navigate through large sets of records efficiently.

limit.description: Number of results per page for pagination. Controls batch size for data retrieval, typically set to reasonable values like 10-50.

oneOf.description: Optional search query to filter results by text fields. Supports wildcard matching for flexible searches.

search.description: Optional search query to filter results by text fields. Supports wildcard matching for flexible searches.

oneOf.description: Field to sort results by. Supported options vary by entity type.

sortBy.description: Field to sort results by. Supported options vary by entity type.

Sorting direction for results. 'asc' for ascending order (default), 'desc' for descending order.

sortOrder.description: Sorting direction for results. 'asc' for ascending order (default), 'desc' for descending order.

IPaginationBase.ICreate.description:
Base pagination and filtering criteria for administrative and list operations.

Provides standardized pagination controls, search capabilities, and sorting options that can be extended by specific entity request types. This base structure ensures consistent querying patterns across different administrative interfaces while allowing entity-specific filtering extensions.

fieldName.description: Database field name to sort by. Common options include 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'name', 'id' depending on the entity being queried.

Standardized sort configuration for database queries and result ordering.

Provides a consistent way to specify field-based sorting with directional control. Used across administrative interfaces and list operations to enable user-controlled result ordering while maintaining database query efficiency and predictable result sets.

ITodoAppTaskCompletionsStatistics.description:
Daily task completion statistics showing completion counts per calendar day over a specified timeframe for the authenticated user.

This entity aggregates completion events from the task completion history to provide daily completion counts and trend analysis. The data supports productivity visualization and helps users understand their daily workflow effectiveness across different time periods.

Daily completion statistics reveal work patterns, identify peak productivity days, and provide insights for optimizing daily routines and task scheduling strategies. Users can leverage this information to maintain consistent completion rates and improve daily productivity planning.

The statistics include daily completion counts along with aggregated totals and trend indicators. The operation queries completion records across defined timeframes while maintaining data privacy through authenticated user filtering.

total_completions.description: Total number of task completion events across all days in the analysis period, representing overall productivity volume.

distinct_days_with_completions.description: Number of unique calendar days with at least one task completion, indicating task completion consistency across the timeframe.

daily_completions.description: Array of daily completion data organized chronologically, providing task completion counts for each calendar day in the analysis timeframe.

average_daily_completions.description: Average number of task completions per day across the analysis timeframe, providing insight into typical daily productivity levels.

best_day_completions.description: Highest number of task completions achieved in a single day during the analysis period, representing peak daily productivity.

best_day_date.description: Calendar date when the best day completions were achieved, identifying the most productive day in the analysis timeframe.

trend.description: Completion trend indicators analyzing the direction and strength of task completion patterns over time.

analysis_period_start_date.description: Start date of the analysis timeframe, defining the beginning of the date range for completion statistics calculation.

analysis_period_end_date.description: End date of the analysis timeframe, defining the conclusion of the date range for completion statistics calculation.

ITodoAppTaskCompletion.ICreate.description:
Request payload for bulk completion of multiple todo tasks. Enables authenticated users to mark multiple tasks as completed in a single atomic operation, providing efficient workflow for bulk task management.

This operation supports productivity patterns including end-of-day task reviews, project completion workflows, and organizational task management where multiple items can be addressed simultaneously. The operation maintains audit trails by creating completion records while updating task status in bulk.

Supports both selective completion (specific tasks) and filtered completion based on user criteria. Atomic processing ensures all valid tasks are completed successfully or none are modified, maintaining data consistency.

task_ids.description: Array of task UUIDs to be marked as completed. All tasks must belong to the authenticated user and exist in the todo_app_tasks table. Tasks must be in pending or in-progress status for successful completion.

ITodoAppTaskCompletion.ISummary.description:
Response summary containing statistics and confirmation of the bulk task completion operation results.

Provides comprehensive feedback about the bulk completion attempt including success counts, failure details, and completion statistics. This enables users to understand the outcome of their bulk operation and identify any tasks that couldn't be completed.

Contains advisory messages and summary statistics to help users interpret bulk operation results and plan follow-up actions effectively.

total_requested.description: Total number of task IDs provided in the bulk completion request. Represents the user's intended scope of the bulk operation.

successfully_completed.description: Number of tasks that were successfully marked as completed. Equal to the number of todo_app_task_completions records created during this operation.

failed_count.description: Number of tasks that could not be completed due to validation errors, invalid status, or system constraints. These tasks remain in their original state.

skipped_count.description: Number of tasks that were already in completed status and thus skipped. Prevents duplicate completion records for already-completed tasks.

completion_percentage.description: Overall success rate of the bulk operation expressed as percentage. Calculated as (successfully_completed / total_requested) * 100 for user-friendly feedback.

completed_task_ids.description: Array of UUIDs for tasks that were successfully completed. Users can reference these IDs to verify which specific tasks were processed successfully in their bulk operation.

failed_task_ids.description: Array of UUIDs for tasks that failed to complete. Users can investigate these specific tasks to understand completion failures and take corrective action.

message.description: Human-readable summary message about the bulk operation results. Provides helpful context and next-step guidance based on the completion statistics.

processing_time_ms.description: Time taken to process the bulk operation in milliseconds. Helps users understand performance characteristics and sets expectations for large-scale bulk operations.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp indicating when the bulk operation was completed. Useful for tracking operation history and correlating with user action timelines.

ITodoAppTaskDeletion.ICreate.description: Request data for bulk deletion of multiple tasks. Contains array of task IDs that will be permanently removed from the authenticated user's task list. Atomic bulk operation ensures all deletions succeed or fail together, preventing partial completion scenarios that could leave task lists in inconsistent states.

task_ids.description: Array of task IDs to be deleted. Must contain at least one task ID for bulk deletion operation. Each task ID must be a valid UUID4 identifier associated with the authenticated user's own tasks to prevent unauthorized access during bulk operations.

ITodoAppTaskDeletion.ISummary.description:
Response summary for bulk task deletion operation providing detailed results including success count, errors encountered, and total items processed. Supports atomic processing where all operations succeed or fail together, ensuring data consistency and preventing partial completion states that could corrupt task management workflows.

The summary structure emphasizes operational transparency by providing complete visibility into processing outcomes. Users receive immediate feedback about which tasks were successfully removed and which encountered errors, enabling effective error handling and recovery procedures. Error details include specific task identifiers and human-readable messages for clear root cause analysis.

This response format supports both bulk operations and auditing requirements through comprehensive result tracking. The structure accommodates various failure scenarios including permission errors, concurrent modification conflicts, and task not found conditions while maintaining clear summary statistics for user interface updates and progress tracking.

Error arrays preserve detailed context about each failed operation, supporting both automated error handling systems and manual review processes. The atomic design ensures users experience consistent behavior where either all requested deletions succeed or the operation provides complete visibility into any partial results, maintaining system integrity and user trust in bulk processing operations.

deleted_count.description: Number of tasks successfully deleted during the bulk operation. This count reflects actual deletions performed and may be less than total requested if some tasks failed due to validation errors, permission issues, or concurrent modifications. Updated atomically to ensure consistency with total processing results and error reporting.

errors.description: Array of error records for tasks that failed deletion, providing detailed information about specific failures such as permission issues, task not found, or concurrent modifications. Each error links to specific task that encountered problems during processing. Errors include both technical details and human-readable messages supporting both automated error handling and user notification systems.

total_requested.description: Total number of tasks requested for deletion, representing the size of the original request batch submitted through the ITodoAppTaskBulkDelete.ICreate operation. Provides baseline for calculating success rates and measuring operation efficiency while supporting progress indicator calculations in user interfaces.

updatedTaskCount.description: Number of tasks that were successfully updated in the bulk operation. Indicates how many tasks had their category assignment changed successfully.

success.description: Indicates whether the bulk update operation completed successfully. Always true when response is returned, false scenarios generate exceptions instead.

message.description: Descriptive confirmation message about the bulk operation results. Summarizes what was accomplished for user feedback.

ITodoAppTaskUpdateResult.description:
Result of bulk task category update operations.

Provides confirmation feedback when users execute bulk category changes on multiple tasks simultaneously. The response includes the count of successfully updated tasks and a confirmation message.

This response type is returned when the bulk operation completes successfully with all requested tasks updated atomically. It gives users clear feedback about the scope of changes that were applied to their task organization.

import { Controller } from "@nestjs/common";
import { TypedRoute } from "@nestia/core";
import typia from "typia";
import { getTodoAppDashboardOverview } from "../../../../providers/getTodoAppDashboardOverview";

import { ITodoAppDashboard } from "../../../../api/structures/ITodoAppDashboard";

@Controller("/todoApp/dashboard/overview")
export class TodoappDashboardController {
  /**
   * Retrieve comprehensive dashboard overview with productivity metrics and
   * task statistics.
   *
   * Retrieve a comprehensive dashboard overview providing essential
   * productivity metrics and task management insights for the authenticated
   * user. This overview serves as the primary dashboard interface for users to
   * quickly assess their task management performance and productivity
   * patterns.
   *
   * The dashboard aggregates multiple data sources to deliver comprehensive
   * insights including current task portfolio analysis showing distribution
   * across different priority levels and categories, completion rate
   * calculations displaying overall productivity achievement and momentum
   * indicators, and due date analysis helping users assess upcoming deadlines
   * and workload distribution.
   *
   * Task statistics provide quantitative measures of user productivity
   * including active task counts organized by priority levels to help focus
   * attention on urgent items, completed task counts over various time periods
   * to demonstrate accomplishment tracking, and category-based organization
   * metrics supporting workflow analysis and project management insights.
   *
   * The overview includes trend analysis capabilities calculating completion
   * rates over daily, weekly, and monthly periods while providing comparison
   * metrics against historical performance patterns. Users receive insights
   * into their productivity consistency and can identify peak performance
   * periods and areas requiring additional focus or workflow optimization.
   *
   * Due date analytics help users manage time-sensitive responsibilities by
   * highlighting tasks due within various timeframes including immediate
   * priorities, upcoming deadlines, and longer-term commitments. The system
   * provides early warning capabilities for approaching due dates while
   * maintaining focus on completion-driven productivity over deadline anxiety.
   *
   * Category-based insights support organizational effectiveness by displaying
   * task distribution across user-defined categories and providing completion
   * rates by project area. Users can identify which areas of their life or work
   * are receiving appropriate attention while spotting categories that might
   * need additional focus or reorganization.
   *
   * The dashboard maintains real-time currency through efficient data
   * aggregation while supporting historical analysis through comprehensive
   * audit trail integration. Users can track their productivity evolution over
   * time while receiving actionable insights that support continuous
   * improvement in personal organization and task management effectiveness.
   *
   * Performance optimization ensures dashboard loading occurs within acceptable
   * timeframes even for users with extensive task collections while maintaining
   * data accuracy and completeness across all presented metrics. The overview
   * serves as both at-a-glance productivity assessment and foundation for
   * detailed productivity analysis workflows.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Get()
  public async overview(): Promise<ITodoAppDashboard.IOverview> {
    try {
      return await getTodoAppDashboardOverview();
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }
}
